original.title: No return to a column after a value departs
original.statement: In a positive-MEX/COPY history, once a value departs from one column, it cannot return to that column. A recovery at another column is a fresh-column MEX event; a value present at or below its row index freezes forever.
assumptions: Full positive-MEX/COPY history; row injectivity for recovery. No UnitDip assumption.

exactAuditedStatement: In a full positive-MEX/COPY triangular history, once value v leaves column c after row s, it never returns there. With row injectivity, a recovery of v at another host at transition q is a fresh-column MEX event with q<=v. If v<=s is present at row s, it persists forever.
hypotheses: Explicit full-history journal V(t, c)={F(r, min(r, c)):r<t}.
COPY iff old value<t, otherwise positive MEX of V and strict current prefix. Row injectivity needed for host-recovery conclusion.
independentDerivationAndChecks: Assume a return and choose least t>s+1. COPY would preserve previous value which is not v, while MEX has v in V from row s because c<=s. Both branches contradict a return; induction not needed beyond least finite counterexample.

At recovery d!=c, row injectivity makes old hostc unique and current F(q, c)!=v. If d<q, old F(q-1, d)!=v so COPY cannot produce v; newborn q also MEX. Hence v absent from entire V(q, d), proving no earlier award in existing part of column. If v<q then old c would COPY v, contradiction; so q<=v.
If v<=s, at next row v<s+1 so COPY preserves it, and induction covers all later rows. No UnitDip, canonical reach, owner-map injectivity, or restriction on movement direction was used.

The additional relay/nonmerging R4/R5 claims in the source have stronger absent-root/endpoint guards and are separate catalogue records; none is needed for R1-R3. No finite counterexample log is used as a proof.
